**Everton (home) vs Ipswich Town in the Premier League, scheduled for May 3, 2025 (pre-match context as of ~May 1-2, 2025).**[[1]](https://sports.yahoo.com/article/preview-everton-vs-ipswich-town-140500803.html)[[2]](https://www.si.com/soccer/everton-vs-ipswich-preview-predictions-lineups-5-3-25)

### Head-to-Head History
Everton and Ipswich have limited recent meetings due to Ipswich’s time in the lower divisions. In their two most recent prior encounters (both in the Premier League era), Everton remained unbeaten. Historical records show occasional competitive matches, with Everton holding an edge in some older fixtures (e.g., high-scoring wins like 5-2 in 1961/62), but no dominant recent pattern in major tournaments.[[3]](https://www.soccerpunter.com/h2h/Everton-vs-Ipswich-Town/13/116/)[[4]](https://m.aiscore.com/head-to-head/soccer-everton-vs-ipswich-town)

### Recent Form and League Context (Pre-May 3, 2025)
- Everton entered the match with a mixed run, including a 0-2 home loss to Manchester City on April 19, 2025 (record around 8-14-11, 38 points at that stage) and a 1-1 draw at home to Arsenal on April 5, 2025.[[5]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/704604/manchester-city-everton)[[6]](https://www.evertonresults.com/202425.htm)
- Ipswich, as a newly promoted side, were battling relegation (likely near the bottom, around 18th in some references) and had shown inconsistency.[[7]](https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cd6jelpxln0t)
- A preview model from late April gave Everton roughly a 59% chance of winning, with a draw around 23%.[[8]](https://www.statsinsider.com.au/news/everton-vs-ipswich-town-prediction-and-tips-4-may-2025)

### Injuries and Suspensions
- **Ipswich**: Significant injury concerns, with reports of as many as 11 players potentially unavailable for the trip to Merseyside. Key names mentioned included Nathan Broadhead (among others). This depth issue was highlighted as a major challenge.[[2]](https://www.si.com/soccer/everton-vs-ipswich-preview-predictions-lineups-5-3-25)
- **Everton**: Jarrad Branthwaite was noted in team news contexts around late April (specific status varied by report, sometimes listed with injury mentions like hamstring in broader updates, though exact pre-match availability needed confirmation closer to the date). Other squad details referenced players like Jordan Pickford and Nathan Patterson in recent lineups.[[1]](https://sports.yahoo.com/article/preview-everton-vs-ipswich-town-140500803.html)

### Venue, Travel, and Home Advantage
- **Venue**: Goodison Park (Everton’s historic home). This match carried major emotional weight as one of the final games at the stadium before Everton’s relocation to a new ground, expected to boost crowd atmosphere and motivation.[[9]](https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/704625/ipswich-town-everton)
- **Travel/Fatigue**: Ipswich faced a substantial journey from Suffolk to Liverpool (roughly 200+ miles one way). While not extreme for a Premier League side, it added to fatigue considerations for a team already dealing with injuries and a tough schedule. - **Crowd/Home Advantage**: Strong Everton support at Goodison, amplified by the farewell storyline, typically provides a significant edge in atmosphere and intensity. No notable pitch, altitude, or climate issues reported for this fixture. ### Other Notable Storylines
- Everton’s survival or mid-table push in a competitive Premier League season. - Ipswich’s fight against relegation as a promoted team adapting to top-flight demands. - Managerial angles (e.g., David Moyes referenced in Everton contexts) and player interest notes (e.g., mentions of Ipswich’s Liam Delap in Everton-related commentary). - Overall, previews framed this as a favorable matchup for Everton on paper, tempered by Ipswich’s potential to cause issues if they overcame their injury woes.[[8]](https://www.statsinsider.com.au/news/everton-vs-ipswich-town-prediction-and-tips-4-may-2025)[[1]](https://sports.yahoo.com/article/preview-everton-vs-ipswich-town-140500803.html)

All details above derive from sources published on or before May 2, 2025 (or clearly reflecting pre-match knowledge). No post-match outcomes or later-season information has been used.

factors.impact: A critically high number of reported injuries (up to 11 players potentially unavailable, including key names) will severely deplete Ipswich's squad depth and quality, making them significantly weaker.

Playing at Goodison Park, one of the final games at the stadium, is expected to create a highly emotional and motivated atmosphere, providing a substantial psychological and performance boost for Everton.

As a newly promoted side battling relegation and showing inconsistency, Ipswich is inherently at a disadvantage against a more established Premier League team, especially when heavily impacted by injuries.
The substantial 200+ mile journey from Suffolk to Liverpool adds an additional layer of physical and mental fatigue for an already beleaguered Ipswich squad.

Late April preview models giving Everton a roughly 59% chance of winning indicate a clear statistical favoritism towards the home side even before accounting for the full impact of Ipswich's injury list.

analysis.reasoning: The combination of factors presents a very strong case for Everton. Ipswich's squad is severely compromised by a reported injury crisis of up to 11 players, which is explicitly noted as a 'major challenge.' This grave disadvantage is further compounded by their status as a newly promoted, inconsistent team battling relegation and facing significant travel fatigue. Everton, conversely, will benefit from a powerful home advantage at Goodison Park, with the emotional significance of one of the final games at the stadium expected to dramatically boost crowd atmosphere and player motivation. While Everton's form has been mixed, they are a more established Premier League side. The confluence of these strong negative factors for Ipswich and strong positive factors for Everton, supported by pre-match models, warrants a significant adjustment in favor of the home team.
